_comment: SLCD-P1-3 shared rejection corpus. Read by BOTH the Go and the Python contract
suites so neither can hold its own private idea of what must be refused.
Each case is a declarative mutation of a valid fixture rather than a second
hand-written payload. A hand-written corpus per language is exactly the shape
that lets two suites go green while sharing one blind spot.
ops:  delete <path>            remove a key (tests required-field enforcement)
set <path> <value>       add or overwrite a key (tests allow-list and bounds)
raw <document>           a literal JSON document (for cases a dict cannot express)
'repeat' multiplies a string value, so an oversize case need not be inlined.
A loader that matches zero cases MUST fail. A green run over an empty corpus
is indistinguishable from a green run over a passing one.
